title: The Poor Rate of 1876
place: Vestry of St Dochdwy's church, Llandough

cast.H_CLERK: the parish clerk entering the Llandough poor rate
cast.E_AGENT: the Bute estate agent, checking Lord Bute's entries
cast.F_GWEN: Gwen, postmistress, waiting with the new directory

shots.direction: Date-and-place card. Exterior of St Dochdwy's church, Llandough, in late-October afternoon light. The church is the newly rebuilt Victorian building with fresh grey stone and a clean slate roof. Damp churchyard, fallen leaves, wooded hillside beyond and the Ely valley falling away inland. A slow push in toward the vestry door, where lamplight shows at a small window. No dialogue; wind and rooks only.

shots.direction: Interior of the vestry, lamplit. The parish clerk sits at a plain oak table with a large ruled rate book open, an inkwell and a steel-nibbed pen. The Bute estate agent stands at his shoulder in a dark frock coat with a leather document case under his arm, reading the entries upside-down. Gwen waits by the door in her shawl, with a thick new directory held against her chest. A slow lateral move across the table. Ambience: pen scratching, clock ticking, rain on the window.

lines.accent: Glamorgan (Bro Morgannwg) Welsh, formal and measured; cy marked for native review
lines.cy: John Williams. Fferm. Perchennog: yr Arglwydd Bute. Tua un erw ar bymtheg a thrigain. Gros: un bunt a deugain, a dim swllt. Yr un fath â'r dreth ddiwethaf.
lines.en: John Williams. Farm. Owner: Lord Bute. About seventy-six acres. Gross: forty-one pounds, and nought shillings. The same as the last rate.
lines.es: John Williams. Granja. Propietario: Lord Bute. Unos setenta y seis acres. Bruto: cuarenta y una libras, y cero chelines. Igual que en la tasa anterior.

shots.direction: Over the clerk's shoulder onto the estate agent. He runs a gloved finger down the column, finds his lordship's entries and reads them back for the clerk to enter. Then he reads the next line.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 medium shot, 1876, pale clean-shaven estate agent in his 50s with thin-rimmed spectacles and a dark frock coat, leaning over a ledger on an oak table and pointing down a column, oil lamp light, a leather document case under his arm, plain vestry interior, period-accurate, invented face, no legible text, no heraldry

lines.accent: Cardiff Welsh, crisp and slightly anglicised, an office man; cy marked for native review
lines.cy: Cywir. Nawr, yr Arglwydd Bute ei hun: coed yn ei law, deuddeg erw ar hugain, tair rwd, a phedwar perc ar bymtheg ar hugain. Yna Daniel Thomas a'i Fab: odyn galch a chwarel.
lines.en: Correct. Now Lord Bute himself: woods in hand, thirty-two acres, three roods, and thirty-nine perches. Then Daniel Thomas and Son: a lime kiln and quarry.
lines.es: Correcto. Ahora Lord Bute mismo: bosques propios, treinta y dos acres, tres roods y treinta y nueve perchas. Después Daniel Thomas e Hijo: un horno de cal y una cantera.

shots.direction: Gwen steps up to the table, puts on her glasses and opens the directory at a marked page. She reads with some pride, then lowers the book and looks from the clerk to the agent.

captions.text: 1875: Worrall's Directory, Penarth section, lists a Williams farmer at 'Great house', Llandough parish.

lines.accent: warm Bro Morgannwg Welsh (Gwenhwyseg colouring); cy marked for native review
lines.cy: Tra'ch bod chi wrthi: y cyfeiriadur newydd, Worrall, oddi ar gert y cariwr. Plwyf Llandochau, adran Penarth: 'Williams John, Great house.' Mewn print i Gaerdydd i gyd. Ac roedd Slater ag e yno yn wyth a thrigain hefyd. Ond shwt mae John yn dal y lle, gwedwch? Ar brydles? O flwyddyn i flwyddyn?
lines.en: While you're at it: the new directory, Worrall's, off the carrier's cart. Llandough parish, Penarth section: 'Williams John, Great house.' In print for all Cardiff. And Slater's had him there in sixty-eight too. But how does John hold the place, tell me? On a lease? Year to year?
lines.es: Ya que están en eso: el directorio nuevo, el de Worrall, recién bajado del carro del fletero. Parroquia de Llandough, sección Penarth: 'Williams John, Great house.' Impreso para todo Cardiff. Y el de Slater ya lo tenía ahí en el sesenta y ocho. Pero decime, ¿cómo tiene John el lugar? ¿Con arriendo? ¿De año en año?

shots.direction: Back on the clerk. He blots the page and taps the rate book with the end of his pen. He is patient but firm.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 close-up, 1876, austere parish clerk in his 60s with a long face and white hair, dark Victorian coat, holding a dip pen over a large ledger and pressing a blotter onto the page, oil lamp light, whitewashed vestry, period-accurate, invented face, no legible text, no heraldry

lines.accent: Glamorgan (Bro Morgannwg) Welsh, formal and measured; cy marked for native review
lines.cy: Mae'r llyfr hwn yn dangos pwy mae arolygwyr y tlodion yn ei godi, Gwen, ac am beth. Dim prydles, dim telerau. Dyna i gyd.
lines.en: This book shows whom the overseers of the poor charge, Gwen, and for what. No lease, no terms. That is all.
lines.es: Este libro muestra a quién le cobran los inspectores de pobres, Gwen, y por qué concepto. Ni arriendo ni condiciones. Nada más.

shots.direction: The estate agent straightens up, closes the clasp of his document case and answers Gwen politely and with finality. He pulls on his gloves to leave.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 medium close-up, 1876, pale clean-shaven estate agent in his 50s with thin-rimmed spectacles and a dark frock coat, standing and fastening the brass clasp of a leather document case, oil lamp light, rain-streaked vestry window behind showing a dim wooded inland hillside, period-accurate, invented face, no text, no heraldry

lines.accent: Cardiff Welsh, crisp and slightly anglicised, an office man; cy marked for native review
lines.cy: Busnes yr ystad yw sut mae dyn yn dal ei dir, nid busnes y plwyf. A busnes yr ystad eleni yw gwaith calch Llandochau. Mae'r plan wedi'i dynnu ar y weithred yn y swyddfa yng Nghaerdydd.
lines.en: How a man holds his land is the estate's business, not the parish's. And the estate's business this year is the Llandough limeworks. The plan is drawn on the deed at the office in Cardiff.
lines.es: Cómo tiene un hombre su tierra es asunto de la finca, no de la parroquia. Y el asunto de la finca este año es la calera de Llandough. El plano está trazado en la escritura, en la oficina de Cardiff.

shots.direction: Insert. The rate book lies open on the table under the lamp, the ink of the new entries still wet. The agent's shadow passes as the door closes. Gwen's directory rests beside the book. A slow push in onto the page, which stays soft and illegible, and the lamp flame steadies. Ambience: the door latch and rain. The captions follow one after another.

captions.text: Later directories (Slater's 1880, Owen's 1887 and 1891, the 1901 Cardiff Directory) also list John Williams at Great House, Llandough.

1876–1912: NLW Bute deeds D153/4–8 cover 'land (33 a.), formerly part of Great House Farm, for the Llandough Limeworks'. Plan engrossed on D153/3 (1875) and D153/4 (1876). The deeds, their parties and the parcel are not yet read.
The same sequence of entries appears in a Llandough rate of 20 August 187? (last figure unread).

continuity: The agent's leather case leaves the vestry for Cardiff. Cut to the Bute estate office in 1877, where the same agent sits at his desk and prepares a notice to quit for Great House Farm, Llandough.
